answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake bond before it can earn: creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital, and the bond is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Think of the shared ledger as a lagoon, calm on the surface, but every new identity drops a stone and the ripple of its cost spreads visibly, while an umber warning flag marks identities that burn bonds repeatedly, so cheap fake swarms drown in their own expense before they can extract value.
